changes.note: A dealer acquisition fee of up to $795 comes off the deal and cannot be passed to the customer — it was nowhere in the record, and $795 is large enough to swallow the flat on a small contract entirely. Also adds the D and E tier participation cap: the record's DFI table has columns for the three term bands but not the separate 2.00% ceiling that applies to every D and E deal regardless of term.

changes.quote: Braun, Delta Leasing, no CB score transactions, vehicles with upfits, and vehicles with greater than 100,999 miles are eligible for the increased back-end but there will be no change to the current all-in-advance
changes.note: Five program notes the record did not carry. The increased-back-end list is the useful one: a high-mileage or upfitted unit gets more room on the back without losing front advance, which is the opposite of what most of the book does. Also that commercial-use deals belong with Ally Commercial Services rather than being declined on retail.

ambiguities.note: The prime advance matrix matches the sheet row for row — 140/135/130/135/125/130 at 63 months and down through the 76-84 band. So do the consumer term limits (84 for new through 2021, 75 for 2020-2016 with the FICO 620 / $5,000 / 100,000-mile conditions, 63 for 2015-2014 on S-B tiers only), the DFI flat scale, the $1,500/$2,000 GAP split at the $80K EDC line, and the 24%/25% new/used rate caps. The 84-month work applied on 2026-08-26 holds up.

Pages 2-7 were rendered but not re-extracted line by line, and the separate Funding Guidelines (10p) and 84-month sheet were not re-read — the 84-month matrix was already extracted on 2026-08-26 and verified against this page. If you want pages 2-7 checked, say so and I will do a second pass.
